title: Best Golf Trousers UK
short: Twelve tested golf trousers for summer and winter, compared on stretch, fit, weather protection and how well they work off the course.
intro: Golf trousers won't save you shots, but stretch, fit, weather protection and comfort make a real difference over a round. This guide compares trousers tested by Golf Monthly's team, who play a lot of golf in them, on the course, on the range and in practice, in rain, snow and sunshine, and off the course to judge how versatile they are. Every member of the team is a regular golfer, and trousers are used over a number of rounds. Eight suit spring and summer and four suit autumn and winter.

products.name: EB66 Performance Five-Pocket Trousers
products.best_for: Golfers who want premium stretch and comfort in a weekend-ready five-pocket design
products.key_spec: Two-way stretch, moisture management, easy care, sizes 30-44, 13 colours
products.summary: Golf Monthly gave these a five-star review: the fabric felt lovely and the trousers stretched and moved perfectly across a variety of lies and stances. They combine technical features with a weekend-ready five-pocket design in an astounding thirteen colours, and feel like a premium product, at a premium price that testers felt is justified.
cons: Premium price, though testers felt you get what you pay for
products.search: Peter Millar EB66 Performance five pocket trousers

products.name: Ultimate365 5-Pocket Trouser
products.best_for: Golfers who want free movement and a familiar casual look
products.key_spec: Stretchy twill, regular fit, mid-rise, recycled and renewable materials, sizes 28-44, 5 colours
products.summary: Golf Monthly found the stretchy twill fabric moves with you, offering unrestricted mobility for every swing, and the five-pocket design is smart enough for the clubhouse and practical for everyday wear. They're lightweight and breathable, which suits warmer days but may leave legs chilly in winter, and the regular fit and mid-rise were preferred over slim fits.
pros: Lightweight and breathable, made with recycled materials
cons: Not the warmest, may feel chilly in winter

products.name: Performance Tapered Fit Trousers
products.best_for: Golfers who want a classic sleek look with a stretch waistband
products.key_spec: Four-way stretch, stretch silicone waistband, side-entry pockets, sizes 30-42, 5 colours
products.summary: Golf Monthly found the stretch silicone waistband means you can play without constantly tucking your shirt in, and the four-way stretch gives great mobility and unrestricted movement in the swing. Their tester wears them regularly for work and on the course and recommends them to anyone who values comfort and style equally, though the tapered fit could feel restrictive for those who like a looser fit.
pros: Excellent mobility in the golf swing
Silicone waistband keeps your shirt tucked in
cons: Could feel restrictive for people who like a looser fit
products.search: FootJoy Performance Tapered Fit golf trousers

products.name: Tour 5 Pocket 4-Way Stretch Straight Leg Trousers
products.badge: Best for on and off the course
products.best_for: Golfers who want tailored trousers they'll wear almost anywhere
products.key_spec: Four-way stretch, straight leg, five pockets, lightweight, breathable and moisture-wicking, sizes S-XXL, 5 colours
products.summary: Golf Monthly called these easily among the very best golf pants you can buy, designed with input from professional golfers to be lightweight, stretchy, breathable and moisture-wicking. The tailored straight-leg fit and back pockets blend in for everyday wear, so they earn their price through how often they're worn, though the straight-leg finish isn't for everyone and they're expensive.
pros: Can easily be worn off the golf course
products.search: G/FORE Tour 5 Pocket 4-Way Stretch Straight Leg trousers

products.name: Tour Repel Slim Fit Trousers
products.best_for: Golfers who want a tailored slim chino with a water-repellent finish
products.key_spec: Dri-FIT fabric, water-repellent finish, gripper tape waistband, sizes 28-40, 4 colours
products.summary: Golf Monthly found a modern, well-tailored slim fit in lightweight Dri-FIT fabric with good breathability and moisture management, plus a water-repellent finish and a subtle herringbone look. The branded gripper tape waistband stops the polo untucking, though golfers with larger legs may find the slim cut a touch tight.
cons: Larger legs may find them a touch tight
products.search: Nike Tour Repel Slim Fit golf chino trousers

products.name: Jupiter 5-Pocket Trousers
products.best_for: Golfers who want an all-day comfortable pair that works on and off the course
products.key_spec: Japanese fabric blend, wide range of motion, lightweight, tapered fit, sizes 30-40, 5 colours
products.summary: Golf Monthly's tester said these might have become their new favourites, competing closely with the Peter Millar EB66. They were comfortable all day on more than one occasion, with a lightweight feel and wide range of motion from the Japanese fabric blend, and subtle branding throughout, though the tapered fit isn't for everyone.
pros: Usable on and off the course
products.search: Sun Day Red Jupiter 5 pocket trousers

products.name: Drive Tapered Trousers
products.best_for: Golfers who want lightweight, water-repellent trousers for most spring and summer conditions
products.key_spec: Lightweight stretch, water repellent, grip waistband, tapered leg, sizes 28-42, 8 colours
products.summary: Golf Monthly found a classically stylish pair that works on the course, in the clubhouse or at work, with modern tapering and a grip waistband that saves re-tucking your polo. They are breathable and lightweight but also repel water, so they suit most spring and summer conditions, though some golfers may fall between sizes.
pros: Water repellent with a grip waistband
cons: Some golfers can fall in between sizes
products.search: Under Armour Drive Tapered golf trousers

products.name: Bowen Tapered Trousers
products.best_for: Hot-weather golf where breathability matters most
products.key_spec: Very light and breathable, internal waistband gripper, light-rain resistant, sizes 29-40, 7 colours
products.summary: Golf Monthly found every small detail carefully considered, including an internal waistband gripper that keeps the shirt tucked in, and called them the perfect summer pair: lightweight, extremely breathable and able to withstand light rain. Front pockets are larger than most, which some will like and others will find less secure than zip pockets, and the light grey shows marks.
pros: Waistband gripper keeps shirt tucked in
products.search: Oscar Jacobson Bowen tapered golf trousers

products.name: ColdGear Infrared Tapered Trousers
products.badge: Best winter, warm and water resistant
products.best_for: Cold-day rounds where warmth without bulk is the priority
products.key_spec: Infrared-tech soft lining, fluorine-free water repellency, 4-way stretch, fleece-lined pockets, sizes 30-42W
products.summary: Golf Monthly found the infrared technology lining insulates superbly well while staying extremely lightweight, and the fluorine-free water repellency lets showers run off. Four-way stretch means an athletic swing is still possible while warm and dry, and the fleece-lined pockets keep hands warm, though the loose fit may not please everyone.
pros: Infrared technology insulates well while lightweight
cons: Loose fit may not please everyone
products.search: Under Armour ColdGear Infrared Tapered golf trousers

products.name: Sensorwarm Winter Trousers II
products.best_for: Cold-weather golfers who want warmth plus plenty of pockets
products.key_spec: Brushed-back 92% polyester, 8% elastane, water resistant, five pockets including a scorecard pocket, gripper waistband, sizes 30-44
products.summary: Golf Monthly found a combination of warmth and comfort for when temperatures drop, with brushed-back fabric that is water resistant, so you only need waterproofs when rain turns very heavy. There's ample storage including a concealed zip pocket and a scorecard pocket, and the gripper tape waistband gives a secure fit, though they may prove too warm in changeable weather.
cons: May prove too warm in changeable weather

products.name: Ultimate365 Arctic Trousers
products.best_for: Golfers who know a round will be cold from start to finish
products.key_spec: Slim fit, stretchy dobby knit, exceptional thermal properties, sizes 28-40, 3 colours
products.summary: Golf Monthly found these keep you extremely warm, to the point that no extra layer is needed on top or underneath, in a slim-fit, incredibly stretchy dobby knit that looks sophisticated. They can catch you out on milder days or as temperatures rise, so they're best when it will be cold throughout.
cons: Perhaps not suitable for milder outings

products.name: Midweight Winter Golf Trousers
products.best_for: Autumn and winter golfers who want warmth without a winter-product look
products.key_spec: Fleeced inner lining, excellent stretch, not bulky, sizes 30-42, 3 colours
products.summary: Golf Monthly's tester calls these their go-to trousers for the autumn and winter season, with a smart design that doesn't give the impression of a winter product and a material that doesn't look cheap or shiny. The fleecy inner lining kept legs warm through a round without bulk, so it was easy to swing on a chilly October day, though those wanting a more athletic fit may prefer another pair.
pros: Not bulky, doesn't look like winter kit
cons: Not for anyone looking for a more athletic fit

guide.q: Do golf trousers make a difference to my game?
guide.a: Golf Monthly says a good pair won't save you shots, but they do have subtle advantages: comfort and flexibility through the swing, practical golf-specific details, and fabrics designed to keep you comfortable and dry while looking smart.

guide.q: What is a waistband gripper and do I need one?
guide.a: It's a silicone or gripper-tape strip inside the waistband that stops your polo untucking during the swing. The Oscar Jacobson Bowen, FootJoy Performance Tapered, Nike Tour Repel and Under Armour Drive here all have one, which saves re-tucking your shirt through the round.

guide.q: Do I need separate summer and winter trousers?
guide.a: Golf Monthly splits its picks by season for a reason: lightweight summer trousers like the adidas Ultimate365 5-Pocket can feel chilly in winter, while winter pairs like the adidas Arctic or Ping Sensorwarm can be too warm on milder days. If you play all year round, one lightweight and one fleece or thermal pair covers most conditions.

guide.q: Which fit should I choose: slim, tapered or straight?
guide.a: It depends on your build and taste. Tapered or slim fits, like the FootJoy, Nike and Sun Day Red here, look sharp but can feel tight on larger legs, while a regular fit such as the adidas Ultimate365 gives a more balanced silhouette. Check reviews and size guides, since Golf Monthly noted some pairs, such as the Under Armour Drive, can leave golfers between sizes.
